extracted.intended_audience: actors, directors, teachers, and writers in theater/television/film; educators and practitioners using improvisation in education, mental health, social work, and psychology
extracted.subtask_description: A handbook of teaching and directing techniques for improvisational theater, covering exercises, workshop procedures, game-based methods, and preparation/rehearsal guidance for adults and children.

rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples listed on the page: Slow/Fast/Normal; Extended Sound; Mirror Speech; Unrelated Conversation. Significance: adds new practice material and introductions for those exercises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Traditional Games for Warm-up (Appendix II)
rubrics_metrics.description: APPENDIX II. Traditional Games — described as 'new section of traditional theater games for warm-up use.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: provides warm-up games intended for preparation and group engagement prior to exercises or performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paul Sills' Sayings of Viola Spolin
rubrics_metrics.description: Included material: 'Paul Sills' Sayings of Viola Spolin' (editorial/illustrative content).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serves as distilled aphorisms or guidance from Spolin (editorial material meant to convey core principles).

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonverbal, Nonpsychological Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Biographical note: Spolin 'began to develop her nonverbal, nonpsychological approach' to stimulating creative expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied pedagogical principle: emphasis on game-based/nonverbal techniques rather than psychotherapeutic interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Games, Storytelling, Folk Dance, and Dramatics
rubrics_metrics.description: Biographical note: Spolin was introduced to and used 'games, storytelling, folk dance, and dramatics as tools for stimulating creative expression.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied methods: incorporate diverse play-based modalities to stimulate improvisation and creativity.
